children: , the consumer-technology and services giant, turned a closed antitrust fight into a new transparency battle after a federal judge ordered X and SpaceXAI to hand over their agreement with Apple, Reuters reported. Apple shares gained approximately 0.2% to $333.09. The valuation picture is already stretched: the stock sits 16.41% above its $286.14 GF Value, suggesting investors are paying a meaningful premium for Apple's current growth and platform economics.

OpenAI wants the agreement as it defends the claims still standing against the company. The dispute traces back to Apple's decision to integrate ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence, although Apple has maintained that its OpenAI arrangement was never exclusive. What matters now is what the documents actually reveal. No payment structure, operating concession or continuing obligation tied to the agreement has yet been publicly established.

That disclosure could carry more weight because Apple's Services machine keeps getting bigger. Services generated $30.74 billion, roughly 28.1% of Apple's latest $109.4 billion quarter. If the agreement changed default positioning, AI distribution rights or access for competing models, investors will have another clue about how Apple intends to defend control of its ecosystem. At $333.09, with the shares already trading well above GF Value, the market is leaving less room for surprises around a business increasingly dependent on high-margin Services growth.

title: Apple Shares Trade 16.41% Above GF Value as AI Agreement Faces Disclosure
